answer: The ripple graph is rebuilt each epoch, as a result the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the pearl audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the prism checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 9 times its size, so a group of 54 keys loses far more than 54 single identities would. That is 10 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
